short: The number of people entering your premises.
metaDescription: Footfall is the number of people who physically enter a shop or restaurant in a period, whether or not they buy. The number of people entering your premises.
definition: Footfall is the number of people who physically enter a shop or restaurant in a period, whether or not they buy. It is the top of the funnel for any location-based business.
bodyHtml:
Why Footfall matters

Footfall separates a traffic problem from a conversion problem. Steady footfall with falling sales points at the offer or the service, not at the location.

Footfall formula

Conversion rate = Bills issued ÷ Footfall × 100

Sales per visitor = revenue ÷ footfall.

How Footfall works in practice

Count it even roughly — a manual counter at peak hours for a week is enough to establish a baseline. Track it against day-part and weather, since both explain more variation than most owners expect.

faq.question: How do I increase footfall?
faq.answer: Visibility first — signage, listings and reviews — then a reason to visit at the specific hours you are quiet.

faq.question: Is footfall useful for a delivery-only business?
faq.answer: Not directly. Listing views and impressions are the equivalent top-of-funnel measure.
